summary: 听音乐可能干扰某些工作任务，但办公室里戴耳机的人仍然很多。文章回顾耳机的历史，解释私人声音空间为何对身处人群的人有吸引力。
logic: 在拥挤环境中划出空间

paragraphs.brief: 在调查后的调查中，人们有信心地报告说，音乐使他们更加快乐，更加集中，更有生产力。
sentences: To visit a typical modern office today is to walk into a room with possibly a dozen songs playing simultaneously but to hear none of them.
今天参观一个典型的现代办公室就是走进一间房间可能同时放十几首歌但听不到
Up to half of younger workers listen to music on their headphones, and nearly all of them think it makes them better at their jobs.
近一半的年轻工人在耳机上听音乐，几乎所有的工人都认为这能让他们在工作中做得更好。
In survey after survey, people report with confidence that music makes them happier, better at concentrating, and more productive.
在调查后的调查中，人们有信心地报告说，音乐使他们更加快乐，更加集中，更有生产力。

paragraphs.brief: 科学家们并不认同这种信念；他们坚持认为听音乐会伤害人们回忆自己应该做的事的能力，而任何流行歌曲，无论响亮还是柔软，都会降低外向和内向的总体表现。
sentences: Scientists do not share this belief; they maintain that listening to music hurts people’s ability to recall other things they should be doing, and any pop song, loud or soft, reduces overall performance for both extroverts and introverts.
科学家们并不认同这种信念；他们坚持认为听音乐会伤害人们回忆自己应该做的事的能力，而任何流行歌曲，无论响亮还是柔软，都会降低外向和内向的总体表现。

A Taiwanese study linked music that has lyrics to lower marks on concentration tests for college students, and other research has shown music with lyrics scrambles our brains’ verbal-processing skills.
台湾的一项研究将歌词与降低大学生集中测试的分数联系起来，而其他研究显示，歌词会干扰我们的大脑语言处理技能。
“As silence has the best overall performance, it would still be advisable that people work in silence,” another reporter dryly concluded.
“沉默总体上表现最好，人们最好还是沉默工作，”另一位记者对此作了口头总结。

paragraphs.brief: 因此，问题是：如果耳机对生产力如此不利，为什么这么多人在工作中拥有耳机？
sentences: The question is therefore: if headphones are so bad for productivity, why do so many people at work have them?
因此，问题是：如果耳机对生产力如此不利，为什么这么多人在工作中拥有耳机？

One factor to consider is that countries like the USA have moved from a farming and manufacturing economy to a service economy, with an emphasis on jobs in offices that require higher levels of concentration, reflection and creativity.
需要考虑的一个因素是，像美国这样的国家已经从农业和制造业经济转向服务经济，重点是那些需要更集中、思考和创造性的办公室的工作。
As an estimated 70 percent of office workers work in open-plan office spaces, it is more important to create one’s own enclosing bubble of sound.
由于估计有70%的办公室工作人员在开放式计划办公空间工作，因此更为重要的是创造出一个带有声音的泡沫。
Lending strength to the argument for headphones at work is evidence that music relaxes our muscles, improves our mood, and may even moderately reduce blood pressure, heart rate and anxiety.
工作时用耳机的争论力证明音乐能放松肌肉改善我们的情绪甚至能稍微降低血压心率和焦虑

paragraphs.brief: 耳机的故事始于1910年，当时美国海军收到一封用紫墨水写在蓝粉纸上的奇特信件。
sentences: The story of headphones began in 1910, when the US Navy received an odd letter written in purple ink on blue-and-pink paper.
耳机的故事始于1910年，当时美国海军收到一封用紫墨水写在蓝粉纸上的奇特信件。

The letter writer, an eccentric inventor and repairman named Nathaniel Baldwin, from the US state of Utah, made what at the time was an astonishing claim: he had built, in his kitchen, a new kind of headset that could amplify sound.
来自美国犹他州、名叫Nathaniel Baldwin的信作者兼修补人，提出当时令人惊讶的说法：他在厨房里建造了一种新的耳机，可以放大声音。

This was an opportune invention for the Navy, which asked for a sound test and then enthusiastically adopted the headsets, later called headphones, and used them in World War I for naval radio communication.
这是海军的一个适时的发明，海军要求进行音响测试，然后热情地采用耳机，后来又称为耳机，并在第一次世界大战中使用耳机进行海军无线电通信。

paragraphs.brief: 耳机的目的是在听众的耳朵里集中安静和私人的声音，这与历史上音乐的社会目的大相径庭。
sentences: The purpose of headphones is to concentrate a quiet and private sound in the ear of the listener, which is a radical departure from music’s social purpose in history.
耳机的目的是在听众的耳朵里集中安静和私人的声音，这与历史上音乐的社会目的大相径庭。
“Music, together with dance, co-evolved biologically and culturally to serve as a technology of social bonding,” Nils L. Wallin and Björn Merker wrote in The Origins of Music.
Nils L. Wallin和Björn Merker在《音乐起源》中写道：“音乐与舞蹈在生物和文化上共同发展，作为社会纽带技术。”

Songs don’t leave behind bones, but evidence of musical notation dates back to Sumeria, 3,500 years ago, and in 1995 archaeologists discovered a bone flute in southern Europe estimated to be 44,000 years old.
歌词不会留下骨头，但音乐标记的证据可追溯到3500年前的苏门亚，1995年，考古学家在南欧发现了一支估计44,000年的骨笛。
If music evolved as a social glue for the species, as a way to make groups and keep them together, headphones have done what writing and literacy did for language – they made music private.
如果音乐演变成一种社会胶水，作为一种让群体和保持它们在一起的方式，耳机已经做了写作和识字语言 - 他们使音乐变得私人。

paragraphs.brief: 马奇是对的；财富可以买到 — — 现代技术可以带来 — — 个人独立，而人们总是在寻求这一点。
sentences: Author and columnist Stephen Marche wrote that separation from other people is one of the first things ordinary Americans spend their money achieving.
作者和专栏作家Stephen Marche写道，与他人分离是普通美国人首先花费金钱实现的目标之一。
It is “a by-product of a long-standing national appetite for independence,” he said.
他说，这是“长期以来国家渴望独立的副产品”。
Americans are not alone in their desire for personal independence and privacy.
美国人并不孤单地渴望个人独立和隐私。
Marche is right; wealth can buy – and modern technology can deliver – personal independence, and it is this that people have always sought.
马奇是对的；财富可以买到 — — 现代技术可以带来 — — 个人独立，而人们总是在寻求这一点。

paragraphs.brief: 事实上，现在人们不听任何东西，而只戴耳机，这已变得相当普遍。
sentences: Dr Michael Bull, an expert on personal music devices from the University of Sussex in the UK, has repeatedly made the larger point that personal music devices change how we relate to public spaces.
英国苏塞克斯大学个人音乐设备专家Michael Bull博士多次指出，个人音乐设备改变了我们与公共场所的关系。
Controlling our public spaces is more important now that more people are moving from the edges of cities to live in urban centres.
控制我们的公共空间现在更重要，因为越来越多的人正在从城市边缘迁移到城市中心生活。
“With the urban space, the more it’s inhabited, the safer you feel,” Bull says.
“城市空间越有人居住，你就越感到安全。”
“You feel safe if you can feel people there, but you don’t want to interact with them.”
如果你能感觉到那里的人，你感到安全，但你不想与他们互动。
Headphones create shields for wearers, separating them from other people and their surroundings.
耳机为穿戴者制造防护罩，使他们与其他人和周围环境隔开。
Headphones have their own rules of good manners; they are like wearing a “Do not disturb” sign.
耳机有自己的良好礼仪规则；它们就像戴着“不要打扰”的标志。
We assume that people wearing them are busy and we should respect their privacy, so now people wear them to appear busy.
我们假设人们穿着它们很忙我们应该尊重他们的隐私所以现在人们会穿它们来显得繁忙
In fact, it is now becoming quite common for people not to listen to anything at all, but just to wear headphones.
事实上，现在人们不听任何东西，而只戴耳机，这已变得相当普遍。

paragraphs.brief: 然而，正如本文开头指出的，虽然科学家们指出耳机对生产力有害，但人们在工作中仍然戴着耳机。
sentences: However, as pointed out at the beginning of this piece, although scientists have stated that headphones are bad for productivity, people still wear them at work.
然而，正如本文开头指出的，虽然科学家们指出耳机对生产力有害，但人们在工作中仍然戴着耳机。
It is not just that headphones create privacy out of public areas, but also that music causes people to relax and reflect and pause.
不仅耳机在公共场所制造隐私，音乐也使人们放松，思考和暂停。
The outcome of relaxation, reflection and pausing at work won’t be captured in minute-to-minute productivity metrics.
放松、思考和暂停工作的结果不会以每分钟生产率衡量标准来记录。
What must be considered is that in moments of extreme focus, our attention radiates outward, toward the problem, rather than inward, on how to solve the problem.
必须考虑的是，在极端关注的时刻，我们的关注会向外扩散，关注问题，而不是向内，以及如何解决问题。
However, with music “When our minds are at ease, we’re more likely to direct the spotlight of attention inward,” Jonah Lehrer wrote in his book Imagine: How Creativity Works.
但音乐“当我们的头脑放松时，我们更有可能把注意力的焦点引向内心”，Jonah Lecher在他的书《想象：创造性是如何起作用的》中写道。
“The answers have been there all along.
“答案一直存在。
We just weren’t listening.”
我们只是没在听。
In a crowded world, real estate is the ultimate scarce resource, and a headphone is a small invisible fence around our minds – making space, creating separation, and helping us listen to ourselves.
在一个拥挤的世界里，房地产是最终稀缺的资源，耳机是绕着我们脑海的无形屏障 — — 制造空间、制造分离和帮助我们倾听自己的声音。

items.en: Young people are easily persuaded by surveys that listening to music is beneficial.
items.zh: 年轻人很容易被调查说服，听音乐是有益的。
items.why: 人们在问卷中报告听音乐能让自己更愉快、更专注，这是他们对调查者的回答。文中没有说年轻人是看了调查后才被说服的。

items.en: Different studies share the same conclusions about the desirability of working in silence.
items.zh: 不同研究对沉默工作的可取性得出相同的结论。
items.why: 不同研究都得出“安静更好”的相同结论，符合题干。

items.en: Some doctors recommend wearing headphones to lower blood pressure.
items.zh: 一些医生建议戴耳机以降低血压。
items.why: 文中说有证据显示音乐或许能略微降低血压。研究观察到的效果，与医生是否特别建议戴耳机，并不是同一项信息。

items.en: Nathaniel Baldwin was a respected government researcher.
items.zh: Nathaniel Baldwin是一位受人尊敬的政府研究员。
items.why: 题干称其是“respected government researcher” 与原文相反。

items.en: The effect of the invention of headphones is comparable to the effect of the invention of writing.
items.zh: 耳机发明的效果与书面发明的效果相当。
items.why: 作者直接将耳机的影响类比于文字，让音乐变得私密。

groups.label: 观点判断 · YES / NO / NOT GIVEN

items.en: What does the writer suggest about a service economy?
items.zh: 作者对服务经济有什么建议？

items.en: When the writer mentions the historical evidence for early music, he is
items.zh: 当作家提到早期音乐的历史证据时,
correct: lending support to the view that music has been important in human history
支持音乐在人类历史上一直很重要的观点

items.en: What does the writer say about the social effects of listening to music through headphones?
items.zh: 作者对透过耳机收听音乐的社会影响有何看法？
correct: It has changed the traditional role of music in society
它改变了音乐在社会中的传统作用

items.en: What does the writer say about personal independence?
items.zh: 作家对个人独立有何看法？
correct: Personal independence is something that can be purchased
个人独立是可以买到的

items.en: Why does the writer quote Jonah Lehrer in the last paragraph?
items.zh: 为什么作者在最后一段引用约拿·勒赫尔的话？
correct: To support the writer’s own view

items.en: Headphones and city living Dr Michael Bull believes that listening to music through headphones has changed the ________ the wearers of headphones have with public spaces.
items.zh: 迈克尔·布尔博士认为，戴耳机听音乐改变了佩戴者与公共空间之间的 ________。
items.why: 回到对应内容“英国苏塞克斯大学个人音乐设备专家Michael Bull博士多次指出，个人音乐设备改变了我们与公共场所的关系”，再按题干要求写出答案。

items.en: Living in the centre of cities is becoming popular, as people become less keen on living in the ________.
items.zh: 人们越来越不愿意住在 ________，市中心居住因而日渐流行。
items.why: 对比指出人们“不热衷于住在郊区”。

items.en: In densely populated city centres, headphones form ________ that isolate people from fellow citizens and from their environment.
items.zh: 在人口密集的市中心，耳机形成了 ________，把佩戴者与其他市民及周围环境隔开。
items.why: 耳机构成把人与环境隔开的“屏障”。

items.en: Wearers of headphones are treated with ________ that other people do not receive.
items.zh: 戴耳机的人会得到旁人享受不到的 ________。
items.why: 因此旁人会表现出“不打扰的“礼貌”。

groups.label: 选词填空
groups.instructionsZh: 阅读带空格的中译，回想正确词项及其字母。

pairs: 第 8 段 · 第 4 句
第 2 段 · 第 2 句
第 5 段 · 第 3 句
points: 题干称其是“respected government researcher” 与原文相反。
回到对应内容“英国苏塞克斯大学个人音乐设备专家Michael Bull博士多次指出，个人音乐设备改变了我们与公共场所的关系”，再按题干要求写出答案。
clauses: Scientists do not share this belief; they maintain …, and any pop song, loud or soft, reduces overall performance for both extroverts and introverts.
“that listening to music hurts people’s ability to recall other things they should be doing”补足 maintain 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 maintain 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。
A Taiwanese study linked music …, and other research has shown music with lyrics scrambles our brains’ verbal-processing skills.
“that has lyrics to lower marks on concentration tests for college students”修饰前面的 music。先认出先行词，再读从句补充的特征。
读到 that 时，回看 music，再把修饰信息接回主句。
lead: Whether wearing headphones at work, or in other areas of everyday life, is a good thing or a bad thing has generated a lot of research and opinion
无论是在工作时戴耳机，还是在日常生活的其他领域，是一件好事还是一件坏事，已经产生了大量的研究和观点
